case_metadata.drug_detail: 2.4 mg subcutaneous once weekly; 4 packages (12 mL) per 90-day mail-order fill requested
case_metadata.policy_pathway: CONTINUATION OF THERAPY — Chronic Weight Management (Adult), Wegovy; and QUANTITY LIMITS APPLY
case_metadata.design_note: Two independent grounds with opposite verdicts. The payer is right about the quantity and wrong about the response. The correct output is neither a full challenge nor a full concession: concede the quantity ground and fix it with a corrected prescription, contest the clinical ground with a computed percentage. The percentage is never stated in the note, so the clinical ground also requires deriving 7.0 percent from the flowsheet.

scope_notes: The quantity limit is a supply rule, independent of the clinical continuation criteria. Satisfying the clinical criteria does not lift it, and exceeding it does not bear on clinical eligibility.

appeal_ground_truth.position_note: Challenge is correct as to the clinical ground only. The quantity ground must be conceded, not contested. An appeal that disputes both grounds is wrong, and so is one that abandons the clinical ground because the quantity ground fails.
supported_claims: The record documents a 15 pound reduction from the weight recorded at treatment start, a 7.0 percent decrease, above the 5 percent continuation threshold.
The member has been at a stable 2.4 mg maintenance dose since 03/16/2026, exceeding the three-month requirement.
Baseline BMI at the start of drug therapy was 36.7 kg/m2, above the 35 kg/m2 requirement.
The quantity requested does exceed the applicable limit and the prescription should be corrected to three packages per fill.
unsupported_claims: That a 90-day fill permits four packages.
That the footnote about 63-day and 84-day fill periods raises the permitted quantity.
That satisfying the clinical continuation criteria lifts the quantity limit.
That the quantity limit is a clinical criterion that can be appealed on medical necessity grounds under this policy.
appeal_ground_truth.correct_next_step: Submit a corrected prescription for three packages per 90-day fill, and appeal the clinical ground with the computed 7.0 percent reduction from the flowsheet. Both actions are needed; neither alone results in coverage.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: Semaglutide was started on December 1, 2025 at a recorded weight of 214 pounds, a BMI of 36.7 kg/m2.
The recorded weight on July 6, 2026 was 199 pounds, a BMI of 34.2 kg/m2, at a height of 5 feet 4 inches.
The reduction from treatment start is 15 pounds, or 7.0 percent of the starting weight.
The member escalated to 2.4 mg weekly on March 16, 2026 and has remained at that dose without reduction or interruption.
Weights are recorded at every interval with no regain: 214, 208, 205, 201 and 199 pounds.
The prescription as submitted requests four packages per 90-day fill.
The applicable three-month quantity limit for this strength is 9 mL, three packages of four pens, per 63 days.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The requested quantity of four packages is within the policy limit.
The member has lost 10 percent or more of baseline body weight.
The member's current BMI satisfies the continuation BMI criterion, which is retrospective to the start of therapy.
The member completed a six-month comprehensive weight management program.
The member failed a trial of phentermine, Qsymia, Contrave, or orlistat.
A travel schedule or mail-order arrangement is a basis for exceeding a quantity limit under this policy.
